## Predict a token {.guided-route-part #guided-part-prediction}

:::: {.guided-route-grid}

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-text-input}

### 02 · From language to tokens

Understand why the network needs numerical representations, then distinguish text, tokens, and IDs that form its discrete input without studying segmentation algorithms.

**Core pages**

- [Why represent language numerically?](language-representation.html)
- [From text to tokens: representing language](text-data.html)

**Optional resources**

- [Tokenization strategies: granularity, algorithms, and trade-offs](tokenization-strategies.html)
- [Unicode, UTF-8, and text normalization](unicode-text.html)
- [Designing and evaluating a tokenizer](tokenizer-design-evaluation.html)

:::

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-representations}

### 03 · From IDs to representations

Identify embeddings and positional information. Compare initial and contextualized states before opening the blocks that turn the former into the latter.

**Core pages**

- [From token IDs to vectors: embeddings](embedding-space.html)
- [Positional encoding: giving tokens an order](positional-encoding.html)
- [Why can the same token have different contextualized representations?](contextualized-representations.html)

**Optional resources**

- [Tensors in a Transformer: shapes and axes](tensors.html)
- [RoPE: geometry, derivation, and limitations](rope.html)
- [Sinusoidal positional encodings: frequencies, geometry, and limits](sinusoidal-positional-encoding.html)
- [Contextualized representations: dependencies across positions and layers](contextualized-representations-advanced.html)
- [Embeddings: from vector representations to search spaces](embeddings-deep-dive.html)

:::

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-computation}

### 04 · Understand Transformer computation

Connect Q/K/V projections, attention scores and weights, value aggregation, causal masking, and the other operations in a Transformer block.

**Core pages**

- [The Transformer in a GPT: architecture and computation](transformer.html)
- [Queries, keys, and values (Q, K, V)](queries-keys-values.html)
- [Scaled dot-product attention](scaled-dot-product-attention.html)
- [Causal masking](causal-masking.html)

**Optional resources**

- [Cross-attention: connecting two sequences](cross-attention.html)
- [Why scale attention scores?](attention-score-scaling.html)
- [Q/K/V: mathematical formulation and variants](queries-keys-values-advanced.html)
- [Multimodal architectures: understanding and generation](multimodal-architectures.html)
- [Hybrid LLM architectures: Nemotron 3 and 3.5](hybrid-llm-architectures.html)

:::

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-prediction}

### 05 · From hidden states to the predictive distribution

Trace the projection from final hidden states to logits and the conditional next-token distribution; interpret its entropy before any token selection or observed target.

**Core pages**

- [Logits: scores before normalization](logits.html)
- [Output probabilities: from logits to a distribution](probabilities.html)
- [Entropy: uncertainty over the next token](entropy.html)

:::

## Use and train {.guided-route-part #guided-part-usages}

:::: {.guided-route-grid}

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-inference}

### 06 · Run inference and generate text

Distinguish prompt prefill from iterative decode, select a token with a decoding policy, feed it back into the context, and stop generation without updating parameters.

**Core pages**

- [Generating text: inference step by step](generation.html)

**Optional resources**

- [Advanced decoding strategies](decoding-strategies.html)
- [Complexity and parallelism in LLMs](llm-computational-complexity.html)

:::

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-context-use}

### 07 · Use and design context

Extend inference to the application level. Explain the effect of examples supplied in the prompt, then choose what information a system passes to the model.

**Core pages**

- [In-context learning](in-context-learning.html)
- [Context engineering](context-engineering.html)

**Optional resources**

- [RAG, memory, and context transmission](rag-memory-boundaries.html)
- [Document retrieval: indexing, retrieval, and ranking](document-retrieval.html)

:::

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-scoring}

### 08 · Score observed tokens

Evaluate the probability assigned to a known target, build a sequence likelihood, and connect negative log-likelihood to cross-entropy without selecting a token or changing parameters.

**Core pages**

- [Likelihood and log-likelihood](likelihood.html)
- [Cross-entropy for a token prediction](cross-entropy.html)

**Optional resources**

- [The mathematics of language modeling](language-modeling-math.html)
- [The mathematical chain of LLM training](mathematical-foundations.html)

:::

::: {.guided-route-stage #guided-stage-training}

### 09 · Learn and update parameters

Connect observed targets to the aggregated loss, gradients, and parameter updates, then to the repeated training loop and validation loss; understand teacher forcing conceptually without making shifted-example preparation a stage of the Theory path.

**Core pages**

- [From token penalties to batch loss](loss.html)
- [Gradients: connecting loss to parameters](gradients.html)
- [The training loop: from gradients to a trained model](training-loop.html)

**Optional resources**

- [Cross-entropy for a token prediction](cross-entropy.html) *(recap)*
- [Scaling laws: parameters, data, and compute](scaling-laws.html)
- [From a base model to an assistant: post-training](post-training.html)
- [The mathematical chain of LLM training](mathematical-foundations.html) *(recap)*
- [Score centering in off-policy LLM reinforcement learning](score-centering.html)

:::
